description: Frontend and API developers need to see exactly what a browser will send as multipart form data, because hidden controls, disabled fields, repeated names, and file inputs often create payload mismatches.

control_state_overrides.description: Must be valid JSON text describing per-control state overrides such as value, checked, selected, disabled, or files. If empty, treat as an empty object. Invalid JSON must produce a parse error state and no preview.

expected_field_list.description: Must be a newline-separated or comma-separated list of expected field names, or an empty string. Names are compared case-sensitively and after trimming surrounding whitespace.

html_form_snippet.description: Must contain a single HTML <form> snippet or a fragment that includes one form element. Empty input is invalid. The tool must parse markup locally only.

selected_submitter.description: Must be a submit control identifier such as a control name, id, or CSS-like path token understood by the parser, or an empty string to indicate no explicit submitter. If the selector matches multiple submitters, this is an error.

submission_mode.description: Must be one of the supported deterministic modes. multipart/form-data computes browser-like multipart serialization metadata and field ordering; form-data-preview-only suppresses boundary rendering while preserving field ordering and inclusion rules.

name: multipart-form-data-inspector
title: Multipart Form Data Inspector
